extracted.intended_audience: NIH study section reviewers and investigators preparing/resubmitting NIH R01-style biomedical research grants (immunology/epigenetics)
extracted.subtask_description: A resubmission (Introduction + Research Plan) for an NIH-style investigator-initiated R01 application in preclinical immunology/epigenetics, addressing prior reviewer critiques, describing Specific Aims, Significance, Innovation, Approach, preliminary data, personnel, animal models, and resource sharing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Significance: FOXP3 is a transcription factor critical to the development, maintenance, and function of Treg cells ... actionable mechanistic insight into 1) the FOXP3 EZH2 protein complex, 2) inflammatory signaling regulating EZH2 activity, and 3) the potential for EZH2-based therapy in IBD represents a critical gap in knowledge addressed in this application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The application must explain how the proposed studies address an important problem, fill a critical gap, and have potential to influence the field or clinical care (e.g., opening new therapeutic avenues for IBD and other immune-mediated diseases). Provide epidemiologic/clinical context (unmet need, prevalence, trial remission rates) to justify significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Innovation: The proposed research is innovative because we investigate the effect of inflammatory signaling pathways on epigenetic complexes in Treg cells, a heretofore-unexamined process ... Conceptual innovations include: 1) the novel role for proinflammatory signaling networks in the regulation of the HMT EZH2 pathway in lymphocytes and IBD; 2) the discovery of the required partnership between FOXP3 and EZH2 in Treg function; and 3) ex vivo genetic engineering of Treg cells to function in the setting of inflammation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight conceptual and methodological novelty versus prior work, and emphasize new reagents/models that enable previously infeasible experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach / Experimental Strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Approach: map interaction domains (1.1), test domain function through assays of gene repression (1.2) and Treg cell suppressor function (1.3) using Co-IP, PLA, luciferase reporter systems, ChIP assay, in vitro suppression assays, and in vivo colitis models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear, testable hypotheses, detailed experimental plans, relevant methods, controls, expected results, sample sizes/replicates, and examples of preliminary success (e.g., published experience with techniques). Include how results will be interpreted and follow-up experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Aims clarity and hypothesis testability
rubrics_metrics.description: CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS that EZH2 plays a critical role in the homeostasis of Treg cells, and the disruption of EZH2 function by inflammatory signaling pathways contributes to IBD. Aim 1: define FOXP3–EZH2 complex role; Aim 2: define signaling network responsible for EZH2 phosphorylation; Aim 3: pre-clinical studies to generate Treg cells resistant to disruptive modifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific Aims should be concise, hypothesis-driven, and structured so each aim tests a clear prediction with feasible experiments and measurable outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary data / Key preliminary experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: Key preliminary data: new tamoxifen-inducible CRE-EZH2 KO animals showing EZH2 requirement in FOXP3+ cells for prevention of Rbhi mediated colitis; mass spectrophotometry and molecular modeling identifying phosphorylated residues; 12 mutant EZH2 constructs and CRISPR/Cas9 EZH2 mutant cell line; evidence of susceptibility to DSS colitis, RNA-Seq and ChIP-Seq overlap of FOXP3 and EZH2 targets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete preliminary results that demonstrate feasibility and support the proposed approaches; address reviewer requests for additional data when resubmitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Productivity / Track record
rubrics_metrics.description: Productivity: Since the last review, 3 additional senior authored manuscripts have been published totaling 10 peer reviewed publications generated through the experiments defined in the first four years of this award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document prior publications and outputs generated from the funded project as evidence of productivity and ability to complete proposed work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feasibility / Justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Justification, feasibility and preliminary data: identification of critical role for EZH2 HMT activity, availability of FOXP3–EZH2 conditional KO animals, published laboratory experience with relevant methods, and existing reagents (adenoviral constructs, CAR transgenic mice) that support feasibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate technical feasibility through prior experience, availability of animals/reagents, pilot data, and established protocols; address potential technical challenges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment and institutional support
rubrics_metrics.description: Our environment in the Epigenetic and Chromatin Dynamics Laboratory combined with the Department of Immunology at the Mayo Clinic makes us uniquely qualified to pursue this objective given collective experience of histone methyltransferase biology, proinflammatory signaling networks, and FOXP3 gene regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe institutional resources, core facilities, collaborative expertise, and how the environment contributes to project success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personnel qualifications and effort (Personnel Justification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Personnel: lists collaborator roles and effort (e.g., Svingen, Technician, 12 person months/year; Xiong, Technician, 3.78 person months/year). Personnel Justification: descriptions of experience and specific responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide CV-level justification of key personnel, explicit person-months/effort, defined roles/responsibilities, and how team expertise matches project needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborations and letters of support
rubrics_metrics.description: Collaborators (e.g., Mustelin, Smyrk, Pasare, Ekker): letters of support confirm willingness to collaborate and provision of unique reagents (EZH2 SET domain mutant, IL6R signaling mutant mouse line, TALEN constructs); some collaborators have 'no measurable effort'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include letters confirming access to critical reagents, expertise, and collaborative commitment; specify any measurable effort or clarify 'no measurable effort' roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate animal models and relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of four new animal models including conditional EZH2 KO mouse line, two inducible EZH2 KO mouse lines, and conditional IL6Rα knockout mouse line; in vivo colitis models (Rbhi transfer model, DSS colitis) for preclinical relevance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose animal models that recapitulate disease features, justify model selection, describe husbandry and welfare oversight (Vertebrate Animals section), and link model outcomes to human relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome measures / Endpoints and assessment methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Colitis severity will be assessed by disease activity index (DAI), blinded histology assessment (histologic activity index with 9 criteria), cytokine expression profile of T cells from mesenteric lymph nodes, and cytokine assessment of colonic supernatants; flow cytometry and multiplex ELISA used for cytokine/surface molecule analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define clear, quantitative primary and secondary endpoints, use blinded assessments where appropriate, and provide validated scoring systems and assays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental rigor, controls, and statistical evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples include blinded histology scoring, reporting of sample sizes (n values), presentation of p-values (p<0.05, p<0.001), use of appropriate controls (IgG independent control experiments), RNA-Seq, ChIP-Seq analysis, and replication across mice/experiments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include appropriate controls, replicate numbers, statistical tests, significance thresholds, and methods for reproducibility/rigor (blinding, randomization where applicable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanistic tests including mutants and rescue experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: Functional tests use domain mutational analyses, mutant EZH2 and FOXP3 constructs (Figure 7), CRISPR/Cas9 mutant lines, and adenoviral delivery of WT or mutant EZH2 to test requirement for EZH2–FOXP3 association; expectation that WT EZH2 rescues and mutants do not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design causal experiments (loss-of-function, gain-of-function, rescue) to directly test mechanism and demonstrate specificity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of state-of-the-art methods and methodological breadth
rubrics_metrics.description: Methodological approaches include CAS/CRISPR mutant cell lines, proteomic experiments, molecular mechanics and molecular dynamics, mass spectrophotometry, linear motif analyses, molecular modeling, luciferase reporters, ChIP, PLA, and in vivo adenoviral replacement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ contemporary and complementary methods to address hypotheses, and explain how each technique contributes to mechanistic insight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pitfalls and Alternative Approaches
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer concern that Aim 3 was 'wide ranging with superficial discussion of pitfalls and alternative approaches' led to streamlining the aim and greatly enhanced Pitfalls and Alternative Approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state potential pitfalls for each aim and provide feasible alternative strategies or contingency plans to accomplish the aim if initial approaches fail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data integration and selection of model targets
rubrics_metrics.description: Integration of RNA-Seq from patient CD4+ cells and existing ChIP-Seq datasets to identify 260 overlapping FOXP3/EZH2 targets; selection of RORA and IRF4 as model targets for mechanistic study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use integrative genomic/transcriptomic data to prioritize targets for mechanistic validation and explain selection criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource sharing and dissemination
rubrics_metrics.description: Reagents, including new cell and animal models, 'will be widely shared with the scientific community'; Resource Sharing Plan(s) section referenced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide explicit resource sharing plans for data, models, and reagents, and reference any deposit or distribution mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission-specific requirements (Introduction to Application)
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduction to Application (for RESUBMISSION or REVISION only): respond to prior review with changes and highlight revisions in the new proposal; address convergent suggestions and individual points not shared by all reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For resubmissions, include a concise introduction that summarizes how reviewer critiques were addressed, lists major changes, provides new data added, and points to revised sections (e.g., highlighted changes).
